catalog_quote: The suprasegmental features of Butuanon, which include stress and vowel length are said to be phonemic. As stress shifts from one syllable to another, the meaning of a word also changes as shown in abúd ‘lash mark, bruise’ and ábud ‘to scatter grain’. Vowel length in the language is brought about by the deletion of /l/ when it is between identical vowels and when it is in word-final position ... There are also words in Butuanon which have inherently long vowels. The latter usually occurs in penultimate syllables as shown in the following examples. masawa /masaawa/ ‘bright mahaba /mahaabaq/ ‘long’ (p. 66) ... The state-denoting verbal roots are generally stressed on the ultima when they function as predicate or modifier. (p. 72) ... two suprasegmental phonemes consisting of word stress / ‘ / and vowel length represented by two identical vowels. ... Word stress in Butuanon is said to be phonemic. Some words in the language change their meanings as the stress shifts from one syllable to another. (p. 98)
world_status: statement found in an open source

All three quoted passages are present word-for-word: (a) "The suprasegmental features of Butuanon, which include stress and vowel length are said to be phonemic. As stress shifts from one syllable to another, the meaning of a word also changes as shown in abúd 'lash mark, bruise' and ábud 'to scatter grain'." and "There are also words in Butuanon which have inherently long vowels. The latter usually occurs in penultimate syllables.. masawa /masaawa/ 'bright mahaba /mahaabaq/ 'long'" (the text; the source itself lacks the closing quote after 'bright'); (b) "The state-denoting verbal roots are generally stressed on the ultima…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is phonemic (contrastive), falling on either the penult or the ultima of the root (abúd vs. ábud); inherent vowel length sits on the penult. Molina gives no default position. The comparative source Zorc 1977 (Butuanon one of 36 Bisayan dialects surveyed) supplies the general Bisayan constraints that also hold for Butuanon: 'All Bs speech varieties except some dialects of Kuy and Tsg retain phonemic accent' (p. 216); 'In all Bs dialects studied, a closed penult is stressed. Thus, stress is predictable from the shape of the form' (p. 218, 8.10.2); an accented open penult is long, the ultima is short except by compensatory lengthening (p. 50, 3.1.3); Butuanon is listed among the eastern dialects with ultima accent in bisayáq (note 4, p. 287). Net: lexical penult/ultima contrast on open-penult words, closed penult always stressed.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in Molina 2021 or in Zorc 1977's Butuanon material.
new_statements.exceptions: Molina: state-denoting verbal roots are 'generally stressed on the ultima' when predicate/modifier (p. 71); compensatory vowel length from /l/-loss (balay > baáy) creates long ultimas. Zorc 1977: accent shifts under affixation (five affix accent classes, 4.2, pp. 64-68; e.g. Ceb, But -an suffix); stress can be overridden by exclamatory intonation (p. 51); Butuanon shows accent shift relative to other Bisayan in items like gahíq 'hard' (Molina p. 63 citing Zorc).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (root/citation forms); Molina's examples are isolated words with acute-accent marking; Zorc notes stress is also a syntactic (word-counting) feature and shifts with intonation (p. 50-51).
new_statements.identity_note: Molina 2021 describes the Butuanon of Butuan City (Agusan del Norte) = butu1244 itself, no dialect split. Zorc 1977 codes it 'But' (Table 2 no. 7, binutwanən, Butuan City area, full data). Molina's article is an abridgement of her 2021 UP Diliman PhD 'Butuanon Reference Grammar' (not online), so the dissertation would carry the same statement in fuller form.

sources.note: Butuanon (But) surveyed with full data. 3.1.3 Accent pp. 50-51: accent = length+stress; accented open penult long, ultima short (Ceb, But báy 'friend' : baay 'house'); all dialects but Kuy: closed penult accented. 8.10 pp. 216-219: all Bisayan varieties except some Kuyonon and Tausug retain phonemic accent (púnuq vs punúq); 8.10.2 closed penult always stressed; But lútuq 'cook' : lutúq 'cooked' accent pairs (p. 218); 4.2 pp. 64-68 accent-shifting affix classes incl. Ceb, But -an; note 4 p. 287: But among eastern dialects with ultima accent in bisayáq. This is the source the earlier scan named…
